title: Usage telemetry convergence protocol for late-emitted fragments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: In several customer incidents we observed late-arriving telemetry records (token counts, chunk completions, and finalization markers) that led to transient imbalances between the live session ledger and the downstream billing pipeline. These late-emitted fragments are produced when intermediate components (proxy, aggregator, or client SDK) buffer fragments and flush them after the session has been considered 'final' by the front-end. The result: temporary over/under charging, quota misestimates, and noisy alerts.

Goal: Design and implement a deterministic convergence protocol that accepts late-emitted usage fragments while guaranteeing idempotent ledger semantics and bounded reconciliation latency. The protocol must preserve monotonicity of per-session usage, prevent double-counting, and provide observability for convergence windows.

Scope: backend metering ingestion + canonical ledger reconciliation + lightweight client SDK marker for best-effort ordering. This ticket covers server-side protocol, ingestion changes, tests, and dashboards. SDK changes will be coordinated in a follow-up.

Non-goals: full offline reconciliation for bulk historical backfills (handled by separate audit job), changes to pricing models.

Success metrics:
- Reconciliation window for late fragments <= 10 minutes for 99th percentile of late events.
- No net overcharge incidents attributable to late fragments after rollout (target 0 for next 30 days).
- Unit tests covering idempotency and watermark advance for 100% of new code paths.

Proposal summary:
1) Introduce a per-session monotonic watermark stored in the canonical ledger: ledger_watermark_offset (integer representing largest final byte/token offset applied).
2) All incoming telemetry fragments must carry an origin tuple and a fragment_range [start_offset,end_offset] and a fragment_id (UUID).
3) The ingestion layer performs an atomic check-and-apply: if end_offset <= ledger_watermark_offset => acknowledge as duplicate (log metric). If start_offset > ledger_watermark_offset + slack_window => accept and advance watermark to end_offset. If overlaps partially, perform deterministic merge using fragment_id ordering and canonical tokenizer length to avoid double-counting.
4) Slack window: small buffer (configured at 64 tokens) to tolerate slightly out-of-order flushes; anything beyond slack triggers revalidation workflow instead of immediate acceptance.
5) For fragments arriving after session-final marker, tag them as "post-final" and route through a prioritized reconciliation queue which applies the same atomic semantics but emits explicit remediation events if adjustments are necessary.
6) Emit convergence telemetry: per-session convergence_state (pending|converged|remediated), time_to_converge, remediations_reason, and delta_credits_applied. These fields feed the billing audit dashboard and alerting rules.

Technical approach and implementation steps: 
- Ingestion: extend fragment envelope in ingestion service to persist fragment_id, origin, fragment_range, and arrival_timestamp. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/meters/pull/312)
- Ledger: migrate canonical ledger row for session -> add ledger_watermark_offset and last_applied_fragment_id. Write migration with zero-downtime pattern (backfill with 0).
- Atomic application: implement compare-and-swap SQL/kv path in ledger worker to guarantee only one writer can advance watermark per session concurrently. Implement fallback via optimistic retry.
- Overlap resolution: deterministic resolution function that uses fragment_id SHA1 as tie-breaker and token-aligned trimming to compute delta tokens to apply. Document the algorithm in code comments and spec.
- Reconciliation queue: separate consumer group for post-final fragments; run at higher priority but limited concurrency to prevent billing spikes. Reconciliation emits synthetic 'adjustment' events to billing pipeline rather than raw fragments.
- Observability: add metrics and tracing spans to cover fragment lifetime. New dashboards: "Late Fragment Convergence" and "Post-final Adjustments".
- Tests: unit tests for merge logic, integration tests simulating interleaved arrivals and partial overlaps, chaos test injecting delayed fragments into staging with production-like load.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Design doc reviewed and approved by PM and reliability (signoffs attached in comments).
- Ledger migration applied in staging and canary with no dropped writes.
- Automated test coverage for the new deterministic merge function.
- New dashboards show convergence median < 1 minute and 99th < 10 minutes in staging under synthetic late-fragment load.
- Rollout plan with a canary (10% of sessions) and rollback steps defined.

Rollout plan:
- Step 1: Deploy ingestion and ledger changes in staging with migration flag disabled. Run synthetic workload for 48h.
- Step 2: Enable migration flag and run canary on internal tenant for 4h. Monitor convergence metrics and billing audit.
- Step 3: Canary to 10% of traffic for 24h. If stable, increase to 50% for 6h then 100% over 3 days.
- Rollback: switch ingestion to pass-through mode (accept fragments but mark as audit-only) and revert migration flag if anomalies detected.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: partial overlaps with different tokenizers produce accounting discrepancies. Mitigation: canonical tokenizer normalization at ingestion; if mismatch detected, route to high-touch remediation flow and alert.
- Risk: contention on per-session watermark updates under high concurrency. Mitigation: implement sharded optimistic batching and backoff; measure contention metrics and tune shard keys.
- Risk: billing spikes due to large retro adjustments. Mitigation: limit adjustment velocity per session and emit controlled billing adjustments rather than immediate large credits/debits.

Related artifacts: design doc https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/METER/late-fragment-convergence-protocol, staging dashboard https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/late-fragment-convergence, PR draft https://github.com/redwood-inference/meters/pull/312, spike notes https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ABC-spike-late-frag.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after incident INC-2026-02. Initial design walkthrough with PM and reliability completed. Action items: shard key proposal, slack_window sizing experiment.

2026-03-11 - Marco Hernández: Implemented prototype for deterministic merge function and added unit tests. Push pending internal review at PR #312. Noticed edge-case where fragment_range overlaps but tokenizer lengths differ by 1 due to normalization; added normalization step.

2026-03-12 - Priya Kapoor (Reliability): Reviewed prototype. Concern about CAS hotspots for high-write sessions (chat multiplex). Recommended optimistic batching with per-session sequence buckets. Marked for follow-up design spike.

2026-03-13 - Marco Hernández: Added reconciliation queue consumer and a simple throttling mechanism to limit adjustment velocity. Deployed to staging under feature flag. Synthetic load test shows median convergence 800ms, 99th 6.2s under baseline; moving to stress tests.
2026-03-14 - Elena Morris (Product): Approved acceptance criteria pending dashboards finalized. Asked to include customer-visible explanation for 'post-final adjustments' in billing FAQ draft.
